variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups; 'three times' means 3 pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube the demonstration grasped. The point for A is never taken from memory; it is found from what the step shows, by the point rule at the end of this instruction. The memory holds only picks_done. Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - The robot is holding the cube if and only if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%); the cube list is irrelevant to this test (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position), and fingers 100% open means not holding regardless of any 'lifted off the table' line. Holding: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube given by the point rule below; if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. Point rule for A. At the first decision step (memory empty), use the demonstration steps shown at that step: find the demonstration frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers about 46-51% open; the grasped cube is the listed cube (from a demonstration frame before the gripper descended) nearest that gripper position, and it is the cube reported 'held in the gripper' in the following frames. Ignore cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is high and 100% open; they are only hidden by the arm. After the demonstration's put-down, follow that cube through the shuffle to the last demonstration frame, tracking jointly rather than frame by frame. (1) The shuffle frames are the consecutive demonstration frames, after the gripper has parked high and 100% open, in which cube positions change by more than a few px. (2) Any cube that keeps the same position (within a few px) through a stretch of shuffle frames is resting during that stretch and is excluded from the matching there; the moving cubes in a stretch are the ones to be assigned (a different pair of cubes may move in a later stretch while the previously moving cube rests). (3) Assign the moving listed cubes in each shuffle frame one-to-one to the tracked moving cubes (never two tracked cubes to one listed cube), and choose, over the whole run of shuffle frames, the single consistent assignment whose total frame-to-frame displacement, summed over all moving cubes and all frames, is smallest. Do not decide each frame on its own: per-frame distances to the two candidates are often nearly equal (differences of a few px or less), a cube can jump 20-30 px between frames, lists are sorted by y, not identity, and the moving cubes may or may not have swapped places by the end (both outcomes occur), so do not assume the grasped cube returns to its old spot and do not assume it ends elsewhere. (4) The grasped cube's position in the last demonstration frame under that assignment is its last position. Point at the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position. At every later decision step where A is chosen, the execution steps shown contain the put-down descent: the frame where the gripper is at table height (below about 0.04) with the fingers opening; point at the listed cube in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) nearest that descent position, since that is the cube just set down and the cube to pick again. Pointing at the listed cube position, or within a few px of it (such as the demonstration's grasp position), is acceptable. Never point at any other cube.

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed pick-ups. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, look only at the gripper in the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if it is raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), write the carried value plus one, no matter what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position); if the fingers are 100% open, copy the carried value unchanged even if a cube line says 'lifted off the table'. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Count of completed pick-ups in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (the last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), regardless of what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position; a 'held in the gripper' line in the execution steps is corroborating but not required). It does not change at decision steps whose last frame shows the fingers 100% open, even if a cube line is flagged 'lifted off the table'. e.g. 1

initial.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and the cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list, the robot is holding the cube: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open, all cubes on the table): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the current table position of that cube); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube.

fields.name: target_cube
fields.description: Position [y, x] of the cube to pick. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the cube that appears as 'held in the gripper' (or disappears from the table list while the gripper fingers are about 46% open), note where it was on the table just before the gripper came down on it, and write the position of the cube that sits closest to that spot in the scene at the start of execution (the cube is set down and the shuffle returns it to nearly the same place). At every later step, if the scene at this decision step lists a cube on the table within about 10 px of the carried value, write that cube's current position; if the cube is currently held in the gripper, copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]
fields.annotation: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked up: the cube that is listed as 'held in the gripper' (or vanishes from the table list while the gripper is closed) during the DEMONSTRATION STEPS, located where it sits on the table in the scene at the start of execution (it is set back down at nearly the spot it was lifted from, and the shuffle at the end of the demonstration returns it there). At every later step the value is refreshed to the current table position of that same cube (the listed cube nearest the previous value, within about 10 px) whenever it is resting on the table; while the cube is held in the gripper the value is left unchanged. e.g. [93, 140]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed pick-ups. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, look at the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if the gripper is raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%) and a cube is held in the gripper or missing from the table list, write the carried value plus one; otherwise write the carried value unchanged. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Count of completed pick-ups in the execution so far. It is 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (the last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers partly closed on the cube (about 46% open, cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list). It does not change at decision steps whose last frame shows the fingers 100% open. e.g. 1

history.critique:
field target_cube, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  SITUATION: At the first decision step the rule said the demonstration's picked cube is set back down and the shuffle returns it to nearly the same spot, so the value was the cube nearest the put-down spot. In two of the demonstrations the shuffle (the frames after the gripper parks high and open, where cubes jump tens of pixels per frame) swaps cubes between spots, twice, and the picked cube ends at a different spot entirely; the cube lists are sorted by y, not by identity. The annotated target_cube therefore named a different cube than the one the recorded execution picks at every step, and every later proximity refresh followed that wrong cube. FAILURE: PREDICTABILITY at the first step (the value written contradicts the recorded pick point), then SUFFICIENCY at every pick step since the subgoal point could not be derived from memory. In the demonstration without a shuffle, two cubes of the grasped colour were absent from the list at the grasp frame, one occluded by the descending gripper and one actually grasped, and the rule's 'vanishes from the table list' cue is ambiguous there. CHANGE: Holds the current table position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration grasped. At the first decision step identify the grasped cube as the cube nearest the gripper's position in the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%), confirmed by the first frame that lists a cube 'held in the gripper'; cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is still high and 100% open are merely occluded. Then follow that cube frame by frame to the end of the demonstration by nearest-neighbour matching (each cube goes to the listed position closest to its previous one, resolving conflicts by the smallest total displacement); its position in the last demonstration frame, matched to the nearest listed cube in the scene at the start of execution, is the value. At every later decision step: if the execution steps since the previous decision step include a frame where the gripper is at table height (height below about 0.04), the value becomes the listed table position, in the scene at this decision step, of the cube nearest that lowest gripper position (this is the cube just picked or just put down, and it is the same cube); otherwise copy the carried value. Example: [85, 109]

field picks_done, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  SITUATION: At decision steps right after a pick-up, the scene showed the gripper raised at about 0.15 with fingers 46% open, but the table list still listed every cube, including the held one at its old table position (the list does not drop a held cube in some episodes). The rule demanded 'cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list', so the count was not incremented and the robot was commanded to pick again instead of putting down. FAILURE: PREDICTABILITY (the memory value could not be derived under the rule as written) leading to SUFFICIENCY failures on the subgoal. CHANGE: Holds the count of completed pick-ups; 0 at the first decision step. It goes up by one at each decision step whose own scene (last frame) shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), regardless of what the cube list says; a 'held in the gripper' line in the execution steps since the previous decision step is corroborating but not required. It does not change when the last frame shows fingers 100% open, even if a cube line is flagged 'lifted off the table' near the gripper. Example: 1

Later, when the execution steps plainly showed a different cube being picked and released than the carried value, the instruction had no rule to correct the value. At any later step, look only at the gripper in the last frame shown: if it is raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), write the carried value plus one, no matter what the cube list says; if the fingers are 100% open, copy the carried value even if a cube line says 'lifted off the table'. the policy prompt for subgoal
  Two rules sent the policy wrong. First, the holding test ('fingers about 46% and the cube held in the gripper or missing from the table list') failed whenever the last frame kept listing the held cube on the table, so after a real pick-up the policy fell to the not-holding branch and commanded another pick; and the ambiguity fallback treated a 'lifted off the table' cube line with fingers 100% open as holding and chose put-down when the task was finished. Replace it with: the robot is holding the cube if and only if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%); the cube list is irrelevant to this test, and fingers 100% open means not holding regardless of any 'lifted off the table' line. Holding -> B: put it down. Second, 'never point at any cube other than the one nearest target_cube' combined with the wrong target_cube forced the wrong cube; with target_cube now defined as the cube the demonstration grasped, tracked through the shuffle by frame-to-frame nearest matching, and refreshed after each pick or put-down to the cube nearest the gripper's lowest point in the execution steps, this rule stands but should add: if the execution steps shown include a descent to table height, point at the listed cube nearest that descent position (it is the same cube as target_cube). Keep the required-count rule: not holding and picks_done below the required number (1 for 'again', 2 for 'two times', 3 for 'three times') -> A at target_cube; not holding and picks_done at or above the requirement -> C: press the button. Add that pointing at the listed cube position (or within a few px of it, such as the demonstration's grasp position) is acceptable. Remove the fallback clause about the table list and the 'cube held or missing' wording.

refused
  One step proposed a new field recording the previous command so that a 'lifted off the table' cube line with open fingers could be disambiguated; this is dropped because the corrected holding test (fingers partly closed vs 100% open) already settles it from what the step shows, so the field would fail NECESSITY. One step asked whether to point at the demonstration's grasp position or the cube's listed position; the two differ by only a couple of pixels and both select the same cube, so no separate rule is needed beyond noting either is acceptable. One step asked that the pick count include picks of a cube other than target_cube; with target_cube corrected this situation no longer arises, and the count already ignores which cube was grasped.

  DELETE this field. Across the minibatch the policy answered 22 of 23 steps without reading it, and the one step where it was the wrong field was a step whose subgoal (put it down) does not need a point at all. The fact it held is recovered at every step that needs it: at the first decision step the grasped cube is derived from the demonstration steps shown at that very step, and at every later pick-up decision step the execution steps shown contain the put-down descent (gripper at table height, below about 0.04, fingers opening), and the listed cube in the scene at that decision step nearest that descent position is the cube to pick. So the field breaks NECESSITY. It was also unstable to fill: when the only cube listed at a holding step was drawn 'lifted off the table' far from the descent, the annotated value became that drawn offset position rather than a table position, and a fresh policy read the descent frame's list instead and wrote a different cube. Drop the field rather than repair it; picks_done is the only field the memory keeps.

Replace it with a rule that never mentions memory for the point. history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  The failure is at the first decision step, where the point for A is taken from the demonstration. The goal asked for two pick-ups of the block the demonstration grasped. The demonstration grasped the middle cube, set it back down at nearly the same spot, and then two of the three cubes were shuffled for several frames while the third never moved. At the end the two shuffled cubes sat within a few px of their pre-shuffle spots. The policy, following the current frame-by-frame nearest-cube tracking, mis-tracked at a frame where the two candidates were 14 and 27 px away, then again at one where they were 18 and 22 px away, and ended on the wrong cube; it pointed at the other shuffled cube. Memory was empty and correct (picks_done 0). This breaks SUFFICIENCY: the step shows all the frames needed, but the point rule as written (greedy nearest cube, frame to frame) is too fragile on frames where the two shuffled cubes are nearly equidistant from the tracked cube's previous position, which happens in most of these episodes, sometimes with a margin under 1 px. Replace the greedy per-frame nearest-neighbour clause in the point rule for A at the first decision step with a joint tracking rule over the whole shuffle: (1) Identify the shuffle frames as the consecutive demonstration frames, after the gripper has parked high and 100% open, in which cube positions change by more than a few px. refused
  The failed first step also proposed two tie-breaks: continue the cube's prior direction of motion, and, when the shuffled cubes finish within a few px of their pre-shuffle spots, assume the grasped cube is back where it was set down. Velocity continuation also fails in this minibatch: in one episode the tracked cube had barely moved in the prior frame, so the predicted position favoured the wrong candidate by a couple of px.
